nodeData.note: How individuals in Kenya get a KRA PIN, file the yearly return on iTax, pay any tax due and avoid penalties. Simple steps for employees, bookkeepers and small business owners.

children.topic: What iTax is and why it matters
children.note: iTax is KRA's online system for registering, filing returns and paying tax. Almost every working adult in Kenya with a KRA PIN uses it at least once a year.
A KRA PIN is your personal tax number from the Kenya Revenue Authority. You need it for a job, a bank account, a business licence and to file returns.

manas.q: What is a KRA PIN?

children.note: You apply for a PIN online on iTax using your ID details. Once you have it, you keep the same PIN for life.
iTax is KRA's website for tax work: you log in with your PIN and password, file returns, generate payment slips and download certificates.

manas.q: What is iTax?

children.note: Filing on time keeps you free of penalties. A compliant tax record also helps when you need a tender, a loan or a Tax Compliance Certificate.
Filing a return means telling KRA your income and tax. Paying is a separate step. You can file on time and still owe a late payment penalty if you do not pay.

manas.q: Is filing a return the same as paying tax?

children.note: The basic rule is simple: if you have a KRA PIN, you file every year, even when you earned nothing.
Every individual with a KRA PIN must file an individual income tax return every year, even with no income (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Who must file an individual income tax return in Kenya?

children.note: Returns for a year of income can be filed from 1 January to 30 June of the next year (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When can you file your individual return for a year of income?

children.note: The deadline for the individual return is 30 June of the year after the year of income (check the current KRA rate). For 2025 income, that is 30 June 2026.

manas.q: What is the deadline for individual income tax returns?

children.note: The year of income for individuals is the calendar year, January to December. You file for last year's income in the first half of this year.
People who are exempt from tax must still file a return and enter their Exemption Certificate Number (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Do exempt persons need to file a return?

children.note: For persons with disability, the first KES 150,000 of monthly income is exempt (check the current KRA rate). They file using their Exemption Certificate Number.
Non-residents do not get personal relief (check the current KRA rate). Their tax works differently, so check with KRA or a tax adviser.
There are three common cases: employment income only, employment plus other income, and no income at all (NIL).
Most employees have only a salary. Your employer has already deducted PAYE every month, so the return mostly confirms those figures.
The P9 is your employer's tax deduction card for the year. It shows your pay and the tax deducted. Ask HR or payroll for it early.

manas.q: What is a P9 form?

children.note: Log in to iTax, choose the income tax return for residents, and enter or confirm your pay and tax from the P9. Then submit and save the receipt.
iTax may show your employer's figures already filled in. Check them against your P9 and payslips before you submit.
If you changed jobs, you need a P9 from each employer. Personal relief is claimed once, so you may end up owing a little tax.
If you also earn rent, business profit or side-hustle income, you must add it to the return and work out any extra tax.
Examples: profit from a duka, a matatu, consulting fees, or farm income. Each source is declared on the return.
Work out profit from your sales and expenses records. Guessing leads to errors that KRA can query later.
When other income is added, the total tax is often more than PAYE already paid. The difference is tax due, paid by the deadline.
A NIL return says you had no taxable income for the year. It is the quickest return to file.
File a NIL return if you have a PIN but earned no income in the year (check the current KRA rate). Students and the unemployed often need this.

manas.q: When do you file a NIL return?

children.note: NIL returns can be filed on iTax or on the KRA M-Service App (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Where can you file a NIL return?

children.note: If you had a salary, even for part of the year, a NIL return is wrong. File an employment return with your P9 instead.
An exempt person files the normal return and enters the Exemption Certificate Number given by KRA.
iTax gives an acknowledgement receipt. Save it as proof of filing. If tax is due, the next step is generating a payment slip.

children.topic: Reliefs and how tax is worked out
children.note: Your tax is worked out using tax bands, then reliefs are taken off. Knowing this helps you check your P9.
Annual bands: first 288,000 at 10%; next 100,000 at 25%; next 5,612,000 at 30%; next 3,600,000 at 32.5%; above 9,600,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the annual individual tax bands?

children.note: Monthly bands: first 24,000 at 10%; next 8,333 at 25%; next 467,667 at 30%; next 300,000 at 32.5%; above 800,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the monthly individual tax bands?

children.note: Personal relief is KES 28,800 a year, or 2,400 a month (check the current KRA rate). It is taken off the tax for resident individuals.

manas.q: How much is personal relief?

children.note: Insurance relief is 15% of premiums on life, education (10+ years) or health policies, up to KES 60,000 a year (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How is insurance relief worked out?

children.note: Tax payable = tax from the bands minus reliefs. Then subtract PAYE already deducted to see if you owe more or nothing.

manas.q: How do you get tax payable from tax on bands?

children.note: After filing, any tax due is paid using a payment slip from iTax.
On iTax, choose to make a payment, pick the tax and period, and generate the slip (check the current KRA rate). The slip shows the amount and a Payment Registration Number.

manas.q: What do you need from iTax before paying tax?

children.note: The PRN is the reference number on your payment slip. It links your money to your tax so KRA can credit your account.

manas.q: What is a PRN?

children.note: Use M-Pesa Paybill 222222 (the unified Government paybill). The account number is the PRN on the slip (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How do you pay KRA tax by M-Pesa?

children.note: Take the slip to an appointed KRA bank and pay over the counter (check the current KRA rate). Keep the bank receipt.
Save the M-Pesa message or bank receipt with the slip. They are your proof if iTax does not show the payment.
Late filing and late payment are charged separately. You can be charged both.
For individuals: the higher of 5% of the tax due or KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate). Even a NIL filer can be charged the KES 2,000.

manas.q: What is the late filing penalty for individuals?

children.note: If tax is paid after the due date: a penalty of 5% of the tax due (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the late payment penalty?

children.note: Interest of 1% per month is charged on unpaid tax until it is paid (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What interest does KRA charge on unpaid tax?

children.note: File by 30 June and pay by the same date. If you cannot pay in full, file anyway, so you avoid the late filing penalty.
Real numbers, step by step. Rates as confirmed on kra.go.ke today; always check the current KRA rate.
Mary earns KES 600,000 a year in salary. Let us work out her tax for the year.
117,400 − personal relief 28,800 = KES 88,600 tax for the year (check the current KRA rate).
If her P9 shows PAYE of 88,600, she owes nothing more. This is a simplified example that ignores other deductions.
Late filing penalty is the higher of 5% of tax due or KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate).
5% × 30,000 = 1,500. KES 2,000 is higher, so the penalty is KES 2,000.
5% × 100,000 = 5,000. That is higher than 2,000, so the penalty is KES 5,000.
Tax due is zero, so 5% is zero. The penalty is the minimum KES 2,000.
Otieno owes KES 60,000 on his duka profit. He files and pays 3 months after the deadline.
Higher of 5% × 60,000 = 3,000 or 2,000. Penalty = KES 3,000 (check the current KRA rate).
5% × 60,000 = KES 3,000 (check the current KRA rate).
1% × 60,000 × 3 months = KES 1,800 (check the current KRA rate).
60,000 + 3,000 + 3,000 + 1,800 = KES 67,800. Filing and paying on time would have saved KES 7,800.
Jane pays health and life premiums. See how the KES 60,000 cap works (check the current KRA rate).
15% × 48,000 = 7,200. Below 60,000, so her relief is KES 7,200 for the year.
15% × 500,000 = 75,000. That is above the cap, so relief is limited to KES 60,000.
Good records make filing quick and protect you if KRA asks questions.
P9 forms, payslips, filing receipts, payment slips, M-Pesa or bank receipts, insurance premium certificates and business sales and expense records.
For a duka or matatu, keep daily sales, receipts for expenses and bank or M-Pesa statements. These support the profit you declare.
Make one folder, paper or on your phone, for each year of income. File everything as it comes in.
Keep your PIN and password safe and private. Never share your password, even with a cyber café attendant.
These errors cause most penalties and KRA queries for ordinary filers.
People with no income think they need not file. They do, and a late NIL return can still cost KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Can you be penalised for a late NIL return?

children.note: Forgetting insurance relief on a qualifying policy means paying more tax than you should. Keep the premium certificate.
Typing pay or PAYE that differs from the P9 can show tax due that is not real, or trigger a query. Copy figures carefully.
If you were employed, a NIL return is wrong. You must declare your employment income.
iTax gets busy near the deadline. File early in the window so problems can be fixed in time.
Submitting the return does not pay the tax. Generate the slip and pay, or penalty and interest will build up.
Businesses have more filings. This map covers the individual return; others have their own maps.
A sole trader declares business profit on their own individual return, together with any salary.
A company has its own KRA PIN and files a separate corporate return. See the corporate tax map.
A business registered for VAT files VAT returns separately. See the VAT map.
An employer files PAYE returns for staff. This is the employer's job, not the employee's. See the PAYE map.
Try each one, then open the bubble for the answer steps.
Wanjiku got a PIN for a job application but earned nothing last year. What should she file?
A NIL return, on iTax or the KRA M-Service App, by 30 June (check the current KRA rate).
Compute the late filing penalty when the tax due is KES 50,000.
Compare with KES 2,000. The higher is 2,500, so the penalty is KES 2,500 (check the current KRA rate).
What paybill and account number do you use to pay KRA by M-Pesa?
Paybill 222222; the account number is the PRN on your iTax payment slip (check the current KRA rate).

nodeData.note: eTIMS is KRA's free system for issuing electronic tax invoices. Almost every business in Kenya must use it, and since 2024 your business expenses only count for tax if backed by an eTIMS invoice (check the current KRA rule).

children.topic: What eTIMS is and why it matters
children.note: Start here: what the system is, who must use it and why your expenses depend on it.
eTIMS stands for electronic Tax Invoice Management System. It is free KRA software that sends each invoice you make to KRA as you issue it.

manas.q: What does eTIMS stand for?

children.note: You can use eTIMS on a computer, a phone or a tablet, so even a small duka owner can invoice from a phone.

manas.q: On which devices can eTIMS be used?

children.note: All persons in business must onboard and issue electronic tax invoices, whether or not they are VAT-registered (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Must a business that is not VAT-registered use eTIMS?

children.note: Companies, partnerships, sole proprietors, associations and trusts are all covered (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Which types of business must onboard on eTIMS?

children.note: People paying Monthly Rental Income tax, Turnover Tax or annual income tax on business income must onboard (check the current KRA rule).
Small informal traders, like a mama mboga or a boda boda business, are also expected to onboard (check the current KRA rule).
Suppliers whose services are exempt from VAT, like a hospital giving medical care or a school, must still onboard (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: Must a VAT-exempt hospital or school onboard on eTIMS?

children.note: Since 1 January 2024 a business expense must be backed by an electronic tax invoice to be claimed for tax (check the current KRA rule). No eTIMS invoice usually means no deduction.

manas.q: From what date must a business expense be backed by an eTIMS invoice to be claimed?

children.note: KRA says eTIMS is free, runs on many devices, has a stock (inventory) module, keeps a record of all your invoices and makes filing returns simpler.

manas.q: Name four benefits of eTIMS that KRA lists.

children.note: KRA offers several ways (solutions) to use eTIMS. Pick the one that fits the size and setup of your business.
A web portal at etims.kra.go.ke where you log in and make invoices in the browser. Good for service businesses with few invoices.
Software you download for Windows or Android. It can handle several branches and tills, so it suits shops and pharmacies with many sales.
A simple web version reached through eCitizen. Handy for small traders who already use eCitizen.
Dial *222# on any phone to invoice. It is meant for individuals and sole proprietors, no smartphone or data needed.

manas.q: What is the eTIMS Lite USSD code, and who is it for?

children.note: An app from the Play Store or App Store for invoicing on a smartphone.
For businesses with their own invoicing or ERP system. The system is linked to KRA so invoices go to eTIMS automatically. VSCU and OSCU are the two integration types.

manas.q: Which eTIMS solution suits a business with its own invoicing system?

children.note: A special solution where the buyer, not the seller, makes the invoice. Covered in its own branch below.
You may register on more than one solution. Each has its own invoice number series, and all invoices show on your taxpayer portal (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: If you use two eTIMS solutions, do they share one invoice number series?

children.note: Onboarding means signing up your business on eTIMS. Steps differ a bit per solution; this is the general shape.
You need an active KRA PIN and your iTax login details before you start.
Decide which solution fits you: portal, Client, Lite (web, USSD or app) or system integration.
Register using your PIN on the chosen solution, e.g. on etims.kra.go.ke or eCitizen. Follow the on-screen steps.
KRA reviews the request; once approved you activate the solution and set up your device or till.
Load your products or services and regular customers so invoicing later is quick. The stock module can track goods.
Make your first real invoice and check that it appears on your taxpayer portal.
The daily work: making a sale invoice and correcting it with a credit note.
Your details, the buyer's PIN where they have one, the items, quantity, price and any VAT. eTIMS adds its own invoice number and sends it to KRA.
Business buyers need their PIN on your invoice so the expense counts for them. Always ask for it before you issue.
Log in, pick the customer, add items and quantities, check the VAT and total, then confirm. Print, share or send the invoice.
A credit note reduces or cancels an invoice already issued, for example when goods come back or a price was wrong.

manas.q: What is a credit note used for?

children.note: A credit note can only be raised from the same solution where the original invoice was made (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: From which eTIMS solution can a credit note be raised?

children.note: You cannot just erase a wrong invoice. You raise a credit note against it, then issue a correct new invoice.
Sometimes the seller is too small to invoice, so the buyer makes the invoice instead.
Where the seller is a small business or small-scale farmer with annual turnover not above KES 5 million, the buyer issues the invoice for them (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: When does the buyer issue the eTIMS invoice on the seller's behalf?

children.note: Buyer Initiated Invoicing is done through eCitizen (check the current KRA rule).
A Nakuru hotel buys KES 30,000 of sukuma from a small farmer. The hotel raises the invoice on eCitizen for the farmer, so the hotel's expense is backed.
Another option where the buyer generates the invoice instead of the seller. KRA offers it alongside BII in the same solution.

manas.q: What is reverse invoicing?

children.note: If you buy from small suppliers and nobody invoices, you lose the deduction. BII protects your own expense claim.

children.topic: Expenses that need no eTIMS invoice
children.note: Some costs are excluded from the eTIMS invoice rule (check the current KRA rule).
Staff pay is backed by payroll records, not an eTIMS invoice.
Imported goods have customs documents instead.
Airline tickets are excluded.
Capital allowances (investment deductions) are excluded.
Interest, and fees charged by financial institutions, are excluded.
Expenses already subject to final withholding tax are excluded.
Services from a non-resident with no permanent establishment in Kenya are excluded.
Remember: pay, imports, flights, investment allowances, interest and bank fees, final WHT, non-resident services.

manas.q: List the expenses excluded from needing an eTIMS invoice.

children.topic: Links to VAT and income tax
children.note: eTIMS invoices feed both your VAT return and your income tax computation.
The general VAT rate is 16% (check the current KRA rate). The old 8% rate on petroleum was deleted by the Finance Act 2023.

manas.q: What is Kenya's general VAT rate?

children.note: VAT charged on your sales invoices is output VAT, owed to KRA. eTIMS records it as you invoice.
VAT on your purchases is input VAT. Keep the supplier's eTIMS invoice as proof for any claim (check the current KRA rule).
Your eTIMS invoices are visible on the taxpayer portal, which makes filling the VAT return easier and helps match sales and purchases.
When working out taxable profit, an expense without a valid eTIMS invoice (and not excluded) is added back, so you pay more tax (check the current KRA rule).

manas.q: What happens in the tax computation to an expense without a valid eTIMS invoice?

children.note: Before paying a supplier, check the invoice is a real eTIMS invoice with your PIN on it.
Wanjiku Supplies Ltd is VAT-registered. VAT is 16% (check the current KRA rate). Follow one sale, one credit note and one purchase.
Wanjiku sells goods for KES 50,000 plus VAT 8,000 (16%), total 58,000, and issues an eTIMS invoice.
Dr Receivables 58,000 / Cr Sales 50,000 / Cr VAT output 8,000. Debits 58,000 = credits 58,000.
The customer returns goods worth KES 10,000 before VAT. Wanjiku raises a credit note on the same eTIMS solution for 10,000 + VAT 1,600 = 11,600.
Dr Sales returns 10,000 / Dr VAT output 1,600 / Cr Receivables 11,600. Debits 11,600 = credits 11,600.
Wanjiku buys stationery for KES 20,000 + VAT 3,200 = 23,200. The supplier issues a valid eTIMS invoice with Wanjiku's PIN.
Dr Stationery expense 20,000 / Dr VAT input 3,200 / Cr Payables 23,200. Debits 23,200 = credits 23,200.
Output VAT 6,400 − input VAT 3,200 = KES 3,200 VAT payable to KRA.
If the stationery had no valid eTIMS invoice, the 20,000 is added back in the tax computation. Profit per books 40,000 − 20,000 = 20,000; taxable profit 40,000.
Errors that cost businesses money or cause trouble with KRA.

children.topic: Thinking only VAT payers need it
children.note: Wrong: all businesses must onboard, VAT-registered or not.
Paying a supplier on a handwritten receipt means the expense may not be deductible.
An invoice without the buyer's PIN does not help the buyer claim the cost.

children.topic: Credit note on the wrong solution
children.note: Trying to credit an invoice from a different solution fails. Use the solution where it was made.
Buying from small farmers without raising a buyer-initiated invoice loses the deduction.
Using an old rate or adding VAT to an exempt supply. Check the rate and item's VAT status.
Chasing an eTIMS invoice for salaries, bank charges or flights wastes time; these are excluded.

Record a credit sale of KES 120,000 before VAT at 16%.
Dr Receivables 139,200 / Cr Sales 120,000 / Cr VAT output 19,200. Balances at 139,200.
A pharmacy pays KES 15,000 bank charges and KES 40,000 for cleaning with only a cash receipt. Which is deductible?
Fees of financial institutions are excluded from the rule, so the 15,000 can be claimed.
Cleaning needs an eTIMS invoice. With only a cash receipt, the 40,000 is added back.
A school buys maize from a farmer with turnover of KES 2 million. Who issues the invoice?
Turnover is not above KES 5 million, so the school (buyer) issues it through Buyer Initiated Invoicing on eCitizen (check the current KRA rule).

nodeData.note: How to run a monthly payroll in Kenya: gross pay, NSSF, SHIF, housing levy and PAYE, the payslip, the journal, and paying and filing on time.

children.topic: What payroll is and why it matters
children.note: Payroll is the monthly job of working out what each worker earns, taking off the legal deductions, paying them and sending the deductions to the government bodies.
Pay staff the right net amount, and pass the deductions to KRA, NSSF and SHA on time.

manas.q: What is payroll, in one sentence?

children.note: The law makes the employer the tax collector for its staff. Money deducted belongs to KRA, NSSF or SHA, not to the business.
Any business with staff: a duka with two shop attendants, a matatu owner paying a driver, or a hospital with 200 nurses.
Topic 1 showed how to log in and file on KRA iTax. Payroll uses the same iTax account to file the monthly PAYE return.
Late or wrong deductions bring penalties and interest from KRA and the other bodies, and unhappy staff. Being on time is cheaper.
The same six steps happen every month. Follow them in order and payroll becomes routine.
Gather basic salaries, overtime, allowances, new joiners, leavers and advances before the cut-off date.
Add basic pay, allowances, overtime and taxable benefits to get gross pay for each worker.
Work out NSSF, SHIF, housing levy, then PAYE, then any other deductions like loans or SACCO savings.
A manager checks the payroll report, then net pay goes out by bank transfer or M-Pesa bulk payment.
Send PAYE and the other deductions to the right bodies and file the P10 PAYE return on iTax.
Post the payroll journal in the books, give payslips, and keep the records safe.
PAYE must be deducted, paid and the return filed by the 9th of the following month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: By when must PAYE be paid and the P10 return filed?

children.note: Gross pay is everything the worker earns before any deduction. It is the starting point for every calculation.
Basic salary plus allowances, overtime, commission, bonus and taxable benefits for the month.

manas.q: What is gross pay?

children.note: House, transport and lunch allowances paid in cash are part of gross pay and are taxed like salary.
Things given instead of cash, such as a company car, free housing or school fees paid for the worker.
Non-cash benefits become taxable when their total value is above KES 5,000 a month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When do non-cash benefits become taxable?

children.note: What the worker actually receives: gross pay minus all deductions.

manas.q: What is net pay?

children.note: Four deductions are set by law. Three come off before PAYE is worked out; PAYE is calculated last.
The National Social Security Fund saves for retirement. Worker and employer each pay 6% of pay (check the current KRA rate).
6% on pay up to the Lower Earnings Limit of KES 9,000, so at most KES 540 each side (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is NSSF Tier I (from Feb 2026)?

children.note: 6% on pay from KES 9,001 up to the Upper Earnings Limit of KES 108,000 (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is NSSF Tier II (from Feb 2026)?

children.note: Tier I and Tier II together cap at KES 6,480 for the worker and the same for the employer (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the maximum NSSF per side each month?

children.note: The employer pays the same amount as the worker on top of salary. It is a business cost, not a deduction.
The Social Health Insurance Fund, run by the Social Health Authority (SHA), funds health care.
2.75% of gross salary, with a minimum of KES 300 and no upper cap (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the SHIF rate?

children.note: SHIF is a contribution from the employee. The employer deducts it and sends it to SHA.
A levy that funds affordable housing. Both the worker and the employer pay.
1.5% of gross pay from the worker, plus a matching 1.5% from the employer (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the Affordable Housing Levy rate?

children.note: Remit within 9 working days after the end of the month (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When must the housing levy be remitted?

children.note: Pay As You Earn is income tax taken from salary each month and paid to KRA.

nodeData.note: How accounting programs keep the books for you: what they do, how they post double entry behind the scenes, how to choose and set one up for a small Kenyan business, and the routines and controls that keep the numbers right. Builds on At-work topics 2 (eTIMS invoicing) and 4 (Excel for accountants).

children.note: It is a program that records every money event once and then builds the ledgers, trial balance and reports for you. You enter documents; it does the bookkeeping.
Accounting software stores transactions and account balances on a computer instead of in paper books. Every report is drawn from the same stored entries.

manas.q: What is accounting software?

children.note: The chart of accounts is the numbered list of every account the business uses, grouped as assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses. Every entry must land in one of these accounts.

manas.q: What is a chart of accounts?

You enter bills from suppliers, schedule payments and see what you owe and when (aged payables).

children.note: Many packages count items in and out, so you know quantities on hand and the cost of goods sold without a stock card.
Some packages run payroll, others link to a separate payroll tool. Either way, the salary journal must reach the ledger. See At-work topic 3 (Running payroll in Kenya).

children.note: A credit purchase of stock posts Dr Inventory (or Purchases) / Cr Payables. Paying the supplier posts Dr Payables / Cr Bank.

children.note: Receivables, payables and bank are filled only through invoices, bills and payments. Avoid manual journals into them, or the customer and supplier lists stop agreeing.
Click any figure in a report to see the entries behind it, down to the original invoice. This is how you trace an odd number.
Cloud software runs in a web browser and stores data on the vendor's servers; desktop software is installed on your own computer or office server.
You log in from a laptop or phone, the vendor runs updates and backups, and you usually pay a subscription. It needs a reliable internet connection.

nodeData.note: Month-end close is the short routine each month where you check, correct and lock the books, then hand the owner a clear report. This is At work topic 6, for people already keeping books in Kenya. It builds on Excel for accountants and Accounting software; next come M-Pesa reconciliation and Bookkeeping for a small business.

children.note: First understand what closing the month means and what you get out of it.
A fixed set of checks and adjustments done after the last day of the month, so the books show the true position for that month. When it is done, the period is locked and reports are issued.

manas.q: What is a month-end close?

children.note: Owners make decisions on these numbers: restocking the pharmacy, hiring, paying suppliers. Errors found monthly are small and easy to fix; errors found at year-end are big and costly.

children.topic: Accrual basis: match costs to months
children.note: Record income when earned and costs when used up, not only when cash moves. That is why the close adds accruals, prepayments and depreciation.

manas.q: What does the accrual basis mean for month-end?

children.topic: The goal: a clean trial balance
children.note: Every account checked and explained, debits equal credits, and nothing left in suspense. From that clean trial balance you build the management accounts pack.
Year-end adds audit, tax computation and full financial statements. A good monthly close makes year-end a thirteenth easy month instead of a crisis.
In this map we follow a small clinic with a pharmacy in Nairobi. It sells for cash, card and M-Pesa, buys drugs on credit, and has staff on payroll.
Start with the easy, hard-evidence items: is everything in the right month, and does cash agree?
Make sure each sale, purchase and expense sits in the month it belongs to. A delivery received on 31 October is an October cost even if the invoice comes on 3 November.

manas.q: What is cut-off at month-end?

children.note: Look at the last delivery notes and the first invoices of the new month. Check stock received and goods dispatched near the date match the right month's books.
Gather bank statements, M-Pesa till and paybill statements, supplier statements, payroll report, petty cash vouchers and the stock count sheets. Missing papers are the main cause of a slow close.
Match the cash book to the bank statement and list the differences: uncleared cheques, deposits in transit, bank charges not yet booked. Book the charges, then the balances should agree.

manas.q: What does a bank reconciliation do?

children.note: Match the M-Pesa till or paybill statement to sales recorded in the system, and record M-Pesa charges. The next map, M-Pesa reconciliation, covers this step by step.
Count the cash in the box with a second person present. Cash plus signed vouchers should equal the fixed float; record the vouchers as expenses and top up the float.

manas.q: How do you check petty cash at month-end?

children.note: Now agree each ledger to its control account and post the month-end adjustments.
The list of what each patient or insurer owes (debtors ledger) must add up to the receivables control account in the general ledger. Investigate any difference before moving on.

manas.q: What must the receivables ledger agree to?

children.note: The total of all supplier balances (creditors ledger) must equal the payables control account. Also match big suppliers to their own statements.
Tick your ledger against the supplier's statement. Differences are usually invoices in transit, payments not yet received by them, or credit notes missing.
A cost you have used this month but have not yet been billed for, such as electricity or water. Book it as an expense now and a liability (accruals).

manas.q: What is an accrual?

children.note: A cost you paid in advance, such as three months' rent. Keep the unused part as an asset (prepayments) and move one month into expense each month.

manas.q: What is a prepayment?

children.note: Spread the cost of equipment, furniture and vehicles over their useful lives. Most software runs it from the fixed asset register; check new purchases and disposals are in the register first.

manas.q: What is the monthly depreciation run?

children.note: Count stock on hand (fully or for high-value lines) and compare to the system quantity. Book the shortage as stock loss and look into the cause.

manas.q: What do you do when the stock count is less than the books?

children.note: Post gross pay as salaries expense, and the deductions and net pay as liabilities until they are paid. Check the payroll report totals agree to the journal.

manas.q: What does the payroll journal record?

children.note: Suspense holds items you could not place yet, like an unknown M-Pesa receipt. Find out what each one is and move it to the right account, so suspense ends the month at zero.

manas.q: What should the suspense account show after the close?

children.note: Monthly tax and payroll items are filed and paid through KRA iTax. Rates and deadlines change, so check the current KRA deadlines and rates on kra.go.ke.
Income tax deducted from staff pay. It is declared on KRA iTax and remitted monthly; agree the return to the payroll report.

manas.q: Where is PAYE filed in Kenya?

children.note: Payroll deductions for health insurance (SHIF), pensions (NSSF) and the Affordable Housing Levy. They are remitted monthly; check the current KRA deadlines and rates on kra.go.ke.
If the business is VAT-registered, the VAT return is filed monthly on iTax. Agree output VAT to sales and input VAT to valid purchase invoices before filing.

manas.q: How often is the VAT return filed?

children.note: Sales invoices go through KRA's electronic tax invoice system (eTIMS). Agree the eTIMS total for the month to sales in your books and explain any gap.

manas.q: What do you match eTIMS invoices against?

children.topic: Keep proof of filing and payment
children.note: Save each iTax acknowledgement and payment slip in the month's close folder. It saves hours when KRA or the auditor asks.
This map gives no rates or due dates on purpose, because they change. Always check the current KRA deadlines and rates on kra.go.ke.
With the adjustments posted, review the numbers and turn them into a report people can use.
Scan every line: is the balance on the side you expect, is it close to last month, can you explain it? A cash account in credit or negative stock means something is wrong.

manas.q: What do you look for in a trial balance review?

children.note: A short monthly report for the owner or board. It usually holds a profit and loss, balance sheet, cash summary and a few key numbers (KPIs).

manas.q: What is in a management accounts pack?

children.note: Income and costs for the month and the year to date, side by side with budget.
What the business owns (assets), owes (liabilities) and the owner's stake (equity) on the last day of the month.
Opening cash, money in, money out, closing cash, plus a short look ahead at big payments coming.
A few numbers the owner watches: gross margin, debtor days, stock days, cash in hand. Keep them the same every month so trends show.

manas.q: Name four useful KPIs for a clinic pharmacy.

children.note: Compare each actual line to budget and explain the big gaps in one plain sentence. Example: electricity KES 18,500 vs budget KES 15,000, KES 3,500 adverse (23.3%) because of a new X-ray machine.

manas.q: What is a variance review?

children.note: After sign-off, close the month in the accounting software so nobody can post to it by mistake. Later fixes go into the next open month with a clear note.

manas.q: Why do you lock the period after closing?

children.note: A simple five-working-day timetable keeps everyone on track.

manas.q: What is a close calendar?

The cost then shows twice, once as the accrual and again when the real bill arrives.

children.topic: Mistake: posting to a closed month
children.note: Changing a month already reported makes the pack wrong. Lock periods and correct in the open month.
Old suspense items hide errors and unpaid amounts. Clear it every month, not at year-end.
If the debtors list and the control account differ, the balance sheet may be wrong and nobody knows which figure is right.

children.topic: Mistake: tax filed from wrong figures
children.note: Filing VAT or PAYE before sales, eTIMS and payroll are agreed leads to amended returns and possible penalties.
Keep one checklist and one reconciliation template, and roll them forward each month instead of starting from blank.

manas.q: Name three ways to close the month faster.

children.note: Set up depreciation, rent release and other fixed entries as recurring journals in your software so they post automatically.
Do bank and M-Pesa reconciliations every week. Month-end then only has a few days of items left.

children.topic: Tip: a close folder per month
children.note: One folder holding every reconciliation, count sheet and iTax slip. Reviewers and auditors find everything fast.

children.note: October water is estimated at KES 6,000 but no bill has arrived by month-end. What entry?

children.topic: Q2: Insurance paid for a year
children.note: On 1 October the clinic pays KES 120,000 for 12 months of insurance. What is the October expense and the balance left?
Dr Prepayments 120,000 / Cr Bank 120,000.
120,000 / 12 = KES 10,000. Dr Insurance expense 10,000 / Cr Prepayments 10,000, leaving KES 110,000 prepaid.
The debtors list totals KES 412,000 but the control account shows KES 418,000. What do you do?

nodeData.note: Checking that the M-Pesa money in your books agrees with the M-Pesa statement from Safaricom. Done often, it catches missing sales, charges, wrong payments and money taken out without a record.

children.topic: What it is and why it matters
children.note: Your till or Paybill holds real business money, so treat it like a bank account and check it like one.
M-Pesa is a mobile money service launched in Kenya in 2007 by Vodafone and Safaricom. Businesses take payments with Lipa na M-Pesa (Till or Paybill).

manas.q: When and by whom was M-Pesa launched?

children.note: Comparing two records of the same money and explaining every difference until both agree. Here: your books against the M-Pesa statement.

manas.q: What does reconciliation mean in accounting?

children.topic: Till = a bank account in the books
children.note: Open a ledger account called 'M-Pesa Till' (a cash/bank-type asset). Money in is a debit, money out is a credit, just like the bank account.

manas.q: How is an M-Pesa till treated in the books?

children.note: Without a check you can miss sales, pay for charges you never booked, or not notice money taken out. Your profit and your cash figure would both be wrong.
The bookkeeper, or in a small duka, pharmacy or clinic the owner. Ideally someone who does not also handle the till money.
Daily for busy tills, at least monthly as part of month-end close. Small daily checks are much easier than one big monthly hunt.

children.topic: Till, Paybill and the key words
children.note: Know the parts of your M-Pesa business account before you start matching.
Customers pay to a till number shown at the counter. Good for shops, pharmacies and clinics selling over the counter.
Customers pay to a business number plus an account number (e.g. invoice or patient number). Helps you see who paid for what.
Safaricom's business terms: the head office or store number groups your tills; the till number is what customers see.

manas.q: What is the difference between a store number and a till number?

children.note: The phone number authorised to withdraw money from the store. Safaricom says the till notification SIM cannot be the nominated number.

manas.q: What is the nominated number on an M-Pesa Business Till?

children.note: A way to receive business money on a personal line. Easy to start, but business and personal money get mixed, which makes reconciling harder.
Safaricom lists USSD *234# and the M-PESA Business App for managing the till and getting statements.
Your M-Pesa statement is the outside record you check your books against.
Safaricom says merchants can get daily, monthly or yearly statements on demand after opting in, also through the Business App.

manas.q: How does a merchant get M-Pesa till statements?

children.note: A typical statement shows a unique code for each transaction (letters and numbers). This is your best matching key.

manas.q: What is the best field to match M-Pesa transactions on?

children.note: When the money moved. Helps match a sale on your POS at 10:42 to the payment at 10:42.
Usually who paid or where money went, e.g. a customer name or a transfer to bank. Helps explain odd lines.
Money in and money out in separate columns. Charges usually appear as their own withdrawn lines.
The balance after each line. The closing balance is the figure you reconcile to.
The routine: get both lists, tick what agrees, then explain what does not.
Download the statement for the period. Print or export your cash book (M-Pesa ledger), POS sales report and any invoices paid by M-Pesa.
Last period's reconciled balance should be this period's starting point. If not, fix the old period first.
Match each statement line to a book entry by code, amount and date. Tick both sides.
Anything left on the statement but not in the books, or in the books but not on the statement, is a difference to explain.
Items that are on the statement but missing from the books (charges, unrecorded sales, withdrawals) need entries in the cash book.
Show the adjusted cash book balance equals the statement balance after timing items. Sign and date it.
Most differences fall into a few familiar groups.
Customer paid but the sale was not entered in the POS or cash book. Add it to the books.

manas.q: A customer paid on the till but the sale was not recorded. Which balance do you adjust?

children.note: Charges taken by Safaricom show on the statement. Use the charge shown on the statement; never guess an amount.

manas.q: How do you treat M-Pesa transaction charges found on the statement?

children.note: Money moved from till to bank. If booked on one date but showing on the statement on another, it is a timing difference.

manas.q: What is a timing difference?

children.note: Someone paid your till by mistake. The money is not yours: record it as owed back, not as a sale, and return it.

manas.q: How do you record money paid to your till by mistake?

children.note: Safaricom may reverse a payment a customer made in error, after contacting you for permission. Remove that sale from the books.
Owner pays school fees or shopping from the till. This is drawings, not a business expense.

manas.q: How is the owner's personal spending from the till recorded?

children.note: Typing mistakes, e.g. 4,700 entered as 7,400 (swapped digits). The difference of 2,700 divides by 9, a classic sign.

manas.q: What clue suggests a transposition error?

children.note: A short table that proves your books and the statement agree.
Part 1 adjusts the cash book for items you did not know about. Part 2 adjusts the statement for timing items. Both must end at the same figure.

manas.q: What are the two parts of a reconciliation statement?

children.note: Charges, unrecorded receipts, owner withdrawals, reversals, wrong-till money and your own errors. These need journal entries.
Timing items only, e.g. a bank transfer you booked today that shows on the statement tomorrow. No journal needed.

manas.q: Which items adjust the statement rather than the cash book?

children.note: Adjusted cash book balance = adjusted statement balance. If not, keep looking; never plug the gap.

manas.q: What must be true when a reconciliation is finished?

children.note: A Nairobi pharmacy reconciles its till at 31 October. All charge figures are illustrative, not real Safaricom tariffs.
Cash book (M-Pesa Till ledger) shows KES 184,600 debit. The statement closing balance is KES 199,360. The difference is 14,760.
Charges KES 1,240 (illustrative); customer sale not in POS KES 3,500; KES 2,000 paid to our till by mistake; owner withdrawal KES 5,000; reversal of a double payment KES 1,800.
A sale of KES 4,700 entered as 7,400 (overstated by 2,700). A KES 20,000 transfer to bank booked on 31 Oct shows on the statement on 1 Nov.
199,360 − 20,000 transfer not yet on statement = KES 179,360. Both agree, so the reconciliation is done.
Each cash book adjustment gets an entry so the ledger is right. Debits equal credits in every one.
Dr M-Pesa charges (expense) KES 1,240 / Cr M-Pesa Till KES 1,240.
Dr M-Pesa Till KES 3,500 / Cr Sales KES 3,500.

children.note: Keep business money off personal lines. Pochi or a personal number mixes things and hides drawings.
Only a trusted person should hold the number that can withdraw. Review who has it.
Get regular statements so you always have the outside record to check against.

children.topic: Return money that is not yours

File each signed reconciliation with the statement. Auditors and KRA queries are easier with a paper trail.

nodeData.note: Simple books for a duka, salon, matatu, pharmacy or small clinic. Keep business money apart, write a daily cash book, keep receipts, count stock, and do a short monthly profit and cash check so you know your profit and tax.

children.note: Books are simple written records of the money coming in and going out of your business. They answer four questions: am I making a profit, where is my cash, what tax do I owe, and can I show a lender my numbers?
Writing down every sale, every payment and every amount owed, on the day it happens, so nothing is lost or forgotten.

manas.q: What is bookkeeping?

children.topic: Know if you make a profit
children.note: A busy shop is not always a profitable shop. Only your records show whether sales are bigger than all your costs.
Books tell you how much should be in the till, on M-Pesa and in the bank today, so you can spot losses quickly.
KRA works out tax from your sales or profit. Without records you guess, and a guess can mean paying too much or paying penalties.

children.topic: Get a loan or SACCO credit
children.note: Banks and SACCOs ask for sales records, bank and M-Pesa statements before they lend. Clean books make the answer easier.
Records show your best-selling items, slow months and rising costs, so you can stock and price better.
Treat the business as separate from you, even if you own it alone. Mixing money is the most common reason small businesses cannot tell if they are making money.
In the books the business is one "person" and the owner is another. The business owes you what you put in and records what you take out.

manas.q: What does the business entity idea mean for a small business owner?

children.topic: Own till, M-Pesa line and bank account
children.note: Use a separate till number or business M-Pesa line and a separate bank account for the business. Do not run shop money through your personal phone.
Cash or stock the owner takes for personal use, like school fees or food for home. It reduces what the business owes you; it is NOT a business expense.

manas.q: What are owner's drawings?

children.note: Decide a weekly or monthly amount to take and record it every time. Taking cash "when needed" makes the books impossible to follow.

children.topic: Stock you take home counts too
children.note: If you take sugar or soap home from the duka, write it down as drawings at what it cost you.
Money the owner puts into the business, like savings used to buy first stock. Record it as capital, not as sales.

manas.q: What is capital in a small business?

children.note: A few simple books, kept every day, are enough for most small businesses. You can use an exercise book, Excel or accounting software (see the Excel and Accounting software maps).
One page per day: opening cash, money received, money paid out, and closing cash. It is the heart of small-business books.
Date, details, receipt or invoice number, money in, money out, and a running balance. Add columns for cash, M-Pesa and bank if you use all three.
Opening cash + money received − money paid = closing cash. Count the till at night; the count should match this figure.

manas.q: What is the cash book balancing rule?

children.note: Fill it in before closing the shop. Memory fails by the weekend, and small amounts disappear.
If the count differs from the book, write the difference as "cash short" or "cash over" and find out why. Never quietly adjust the figures.
Every payment needs a paper or electronic proof. File them by month in an envelope or folder, or photograph them the same day.
Receipts, invoices, M-Pesa messages and bank slips are the proof behind every line in your books.

manas.q: What is a source document?

children.note: An eTIMS invoice is a tax invoice made through KRA's system. Ask suppliers for one; it proves your purchase to KRA (see the eTIMS invoicing map).
Use a receipt book with printed numbers so a missing receipt is easy to spot.
A small fixed cash float kept apart from the till for tiny costs like boda fares, milk or photocopies.
A fixed float amount, for example KES 5,000. Spend from it with a voucher for each payment, then top it back up to the same amount.

manas.q: What is the imprest system?

children.note: A small slip saying date, what was bought, amount and who took the money. Staple the receipt to it.
At top-up time cash left + vouchers must equal the float. You refill only the total of the vouchers.
Treat your till number or business M-Pesa line like a second cash box with its own column and balance.

children.topic: M-Pesa column in the cash book
children.note: Record each M-Pesa sale and payment with the transaction code. Charges and withdrawal fees are business costs.
Each week download the M-Pesa and bank statements and tick every line against your book (see the M-Pesa reconciliation map).

manas.q: Why compare your books with the M-Pesa statement?

children.note: Taking till cash to the bank is not a cost or a sale. Show it as money out of cash and money into bank.

children.topic: Who owes whom, and your stock
children.note: Many small businesses sell on credit and buy on credit. Keep simple lists so no money is forgotten, and count stock so you know your real profit.
A page per customer, or one list, showing what they took, when, and what they have paid. Also called accounts receivable.

manas.q: Who are debtors?

children.note: A list of suppliers you owe, with invoice numbers and due dates, so you pay on time and are not charged twice. Also called accounts payable.

manas.q: Who are creditors?

children.note: Review the debtors list each week. A debt older than 30 days needs a call; stop new credit to customers who do not pay.
Count everything on the shelves and in the store at month-end, and value it at what you paid, not the selling price.
Use the buying price (or lower if damaged or expired). This follows the idea in IAS 2 Inventories and IFRS for SMEs.

manas.q: At what value do you count stock for your books?

children.note: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases − closing stock. Without a count you cannot know your true profit.

manas.q: What is the formula for cost of goods sold?

children.note: If stock is lower than records say, you may have theft, damage, expiry or unrecorded drawings. Pharmacies should also check expiry dates.
Small businesses in Kenya mostly meet three taxes: turnover tax, normal income tax and VAT. Which applies depends on your sales. Rates change, so always check KRA.
A simple tax on gross sales for resident businesses with turnover above KES 1 million and not above KES 25 million a year. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: Which businesses fall under turnover tax?

children.note: TOT is 1.5% of gross sales from 1 July 2023 (Finance Act 2023). No expenses are deducted and it is a final tax. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the turnover tax rate?

children.note: File the TOT return and pay by the 20th of the month after the tax period, on iTax or the M-Service App (see the Filing on iTax map). (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Not for rental income, management, professional or training fees, income already taxed by final withholding tax, or non-residents. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
A business can leave TOT by giving KRA written notice, and then pays normal income tax on profit instead. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
If you are not on TOT (or opt out), you pay income tax on profit: sales minus allowable expenses. This needs fuller books (see the Filing on iTax map).
If your taxable sales reach KES 5 million or more in a year you must register for VAT. Below that, registration is voluntary under conditions. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: At what yearly sales must a Kenyan business register for VAT?

children.note: The general VAT rate is 16%. You pay output VAT on sales minus input VAT on purchases, by the 20th of the next month. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the general VAT rate in Kenya?

children.note: A TOT business whose vatable sales reach KES 5 million must also register for VAT. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
VAT-registered businesses must issue invoices through eTIMS. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

The Tax Procedures Act, section 23, says keep records in an official language (English or Kiswahili), in KES, for 5 years after the end of the period they relate to. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How long must a Kenyan business keep its records?

children.note: TOT: late filing KES 1,000 per month; late payment 5% plus interest of 1% per month. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What are the penalties for late turnover tax?

children.topic: A Kibera duka's week of cash
children.note: Amina runs a duka in Kibera. Here is her cash book for one week, day by day.
Amina counts KES 4,000 in her Kibera duka box on Monday morning. All sales this week are in cash.
Start 4,000 + cash sales 6,200 − paid out 3,500 (stock (bread, milk) 3,500) = 6,700 in the box at night.
Start 6,700 + cash sales 5,800 − paid out 2,000 (stock (sugar, flour) 2,000) = 10,500 in the box at night.
Start 10,500 + cash sales 7,100 − paid out 4,400 (stock (soap, oil) 4,000, boda transport 400) = 13,200 in the box at night.
Start 13,200 + cash sales 6,500 − paid out 1,000 (electricity tokens 1,000) = 18,700 in the box at night.
Start 18,700 + cash sales 8,300 − paid out 5,500 (stock (soda, eggs) 5,500) = 21,500 in the box at night.
Start 21,500 + cash sales 9,400 − paid out 5,000 (helper wage 3,000, owner drawings 2,000) = 25,900 in the box at night.
Start 25,900 + cash sales 4,700 − paid out 10,000 (cash taken to the bank 10,000) = 20,600 in the box at night.
Opening 4,000 + receipts 48,000 − payments 31,400 = closing 20,600. It matches Sunday night's count, so the week balances.
The KES 2,000 on Saturday left the cash box, so it is in the cash book. But in the profit-and-loss it is drawings, not an expense.
On Saturday Amina takes KES 2,000 from the box for school fees. Dr Drawings 2,000 / Cr Cash 2,000. Debits equal credits.
Drawings reduce what the business owes the owner. Debit Drawings shows money taken out; credit Cash shows the box got smaller.
Amina takes soap that cost KES 300 for home use: Dr Drawings 300 / Cr Purchases 300. It is not a sale.

children.topic: A month's simple profit and loss
children.note: Amina's duka for October 2026, using her cash book, stock counts and receipts.
Sales 180,000. Cost of goods sold: opening stock 40,000 + purchases 120,000 − closing stock 35,000 = 125,000. Gross profit 180,000 − 125,000 = 55,000.
Expenses: rent 8,000, helper wages 12,000, electricity 1,500, transport 3,000, m-pesa and bank charges 700 = 25,200. Net profit 55,000 − 25,200 = 29,800.

children.topic: Drawings stay out of the P&L
children.note: Amina took 8,000 in drawings in October. It is not in the expenses, so profit stays 29,800.

Opening cash and M-Pesa 15,000 + money in 186,000 (sales 180,000 + a debtor paid 6,000) − money out 153,200 (purchases 120,000, expenses 25,200, drawings 8,000) = closing 47,800. Profit and cash differ because of stock, credit and drawings.

children.topic: Turnover tax for the month: KES 2,700
children.note: Gross sales 180,000 × 1.5% = 2,700. No expenses are deducted. Yearly sales of about 2,160,000 are within the TOT band and below the VAT line. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Float 5,000. Vouchers: milk for tea 600, cleaning 1,200, boda 850, photocopies 300, nails and tape 900 = 3,850. Cash left 1,150. 1,150 + 3,850 = 5,000, so top up 3,850.
Amina's list: Mama Wanjiku 1,800, Otieno (matatu crew) 2,500, Clinic next door 4,200. Total owed to her: KES 8,500.
A short, steady routine beats a big clean-up once a year. Learn the usual mistakes and test yourself.
Small jobs done daily, weekly and monthly (see the Month-end close map for the bigger version).
Write all sales and payments in the cash book, count the till, file receipts, and note credit sales and drawings.

manas.q: What should a small business owner do every day for the books?

children.note: Tick M-Pesa and bank statements against the book, top up petty cash, chase debtors, and check what you owe suppliers.

manas.q: What are the weekly bookkeeping jobs?

children.note: Count stock, prepare a simple P&L and cash summary, and file and pay tax by the 20th.

manas.q: What are the monthly bookkeeping jobs?

children.note: Add up the 12 months, file the yearly return, and store the year's records safely for at least 5 years.
These cause most of the trouble in small-business books.
Paying rent at home from the till without writing it down. Fix: separate accounts and record drawings.
This makes profit look smaller than it really is and gives wrong tax figures.
Without proof, KRA and lenders may not accept the cost. Always ask for a receipt or eTIMS invoice.
Transaction and withdrawal fees add up over a month. Record them from the statement.
Without it you cannot know cost of goods sold, so the profit figure is a guess.
A full box of cash may include money you owe suppliers. Profit and cash are different numbers.
Late returns and payments bring penalties and interest even when the tax is small.
A salon has gross sales of KES 95,000 in a month and is on TOT. What TOT is due?
TOT is on sales before any costs, so use KES 95,000.
95,000 × 1.5% = 1,425, due by the 20th of the next month. (check the current KRA rate; checked 8 Nov 2026)
Opening cash 3,000, money received 12,500, money paid 9,800. What should the till hold?
3,000 + 12,500 − 9,800 = 5,700. If the count is lower, record cash short and investigate.
A pharmacy: sales 60,000, cost of goods sold 38,000, expenses 9,500, drawings 5,000. Find net profit.
Drawings are not an expense, so ignore the 5,000.

nodeData.note: Petty cash is a small box of cash kept at the office for tiny everyday payments. This map shows how to set it up on the imprest system, record it in an analysed petty cash book, post it, count it and stop it leaking. It builds on the petty cash book in (CA11 · Books of prime entry).

children.topic: 1. What petty cash is and why
children.note: Small payments are too many and too tiny to pay by cheque or bank transfer. A small cash fund handles them, with one person in charge.
A small amount of cash kept on the premises to pay for minor expenses such as fares, tea, postage and cleaning items.

manas.q: What is petty cash?

children.topic: Why not pay everything from the bank?
children.note: Bank transfers for KES 300 cost time and charges, and the main cashier stays free for big payments. Petty cash keeps small spends quick but still recorded.
Boda boda or matatu fares, milk and tea, courier parcels, photocopying, cleaning items, small repairs and water refills.

children.topic: Builds on CA11 books of prime entry
children.note: The petty cash book is a book of prime entry, as studied in (CA11 · Books of prime entry). Here we use it the way an office really does.
The most common way to run petty cash. You start with a fixed amount (the float) and top it up by exactly what was spent.
A fixed cash float is set. At the end of each period the custodian is given exactly the amount spent, so the fund returns to the fixed figure.

manas.q: What is the imprest system?

children.note: The fixed amount the fund always starts each period with, for example KES 20,000.

manas.q: What is the float or imprest amount?

children.note: Reimbursement = total of vouchers paid in the period. Cash left + top-up = the float again.

manas.q: Under the imprest system, how much is the top-up?

children.note: At any moment, cash in the box plus the vouchers paid must add up to the float. If not, money is missing or a voucher is lost.

manas.q: At any time, what should cash plus vouchers equal?

children.note: If the float is too small or too big, management approves a new amount. Raising it: Dr Petty cash / Cr Bank for the increase.
Some firms give a set sum each week whatever was spent. It is weaker, because the balance drifts and nobody sees it reset.

manas.q: How does a non-imprest petty cash system differ?

children.note: Decide who holds it, how big it is, what it may pay for and where it is kept. Put this in a short written policy.
One named person is responsible for the cash. One person per box, so a shortage can be traced.

manas.q: Who is the petty cash custodian?

children.note: Look at what small spends usually total in a week or two, then add a little margin. Too big invites theft; too small means constant top-ups.
Set a maximum per payment, for example KES 5,000. Anything bigger goes through normal purchases and the bank.

manas.q: Why set a limit per petty cash payment?

children.topic: What petty cash may NOT pay
children.note: No salaries, salary advances, personal loans, or big supplier bills. Those need the normal approval and payroll routes.
Keep cash in a locked box inside a locked drawer or safe. Only the custodian holds the key; a spare is sealed with a manager.
Cash a cheque or withdraw for the float. Dr Petty cash KES 20,000 / Cr Bank KES 20,000.

manas.q: What is the entry to set up a petty cash float?

children.note: Every shilling out needs a voucher, signed, approved and backed by a receipt. No voucher, no payment.
A small numbered form showing date, amount, purpose, who received the cash and who approved it.

manas.q: What is a petty cash voucher?

children.note: Use vouchers numbered in order so a missing one shows up at once.

manas.q: Why should petty cash vouchers be pre-numbered?

children.note: Staple the supplier's receipt to the voucher. Fares with no receipt need a clear note and a manager's signature.
KRA generally expects electronic tax invoices to back expenses claimed for tax. Ask suppliers for an eTIMS receipt and check KRA's eTIMS rules.
If cash goes out before the receipt, write an IOU voucher. Clear it within days with the receipt and any change.
Stamp vouchers 'PAID' once reimbursed so they cannot be claimed twice.
A petty cash book with extra columns that split spending by type, so totals post straight to the ledger.
A petty cash book with a total column plus analysis columns, one per expense type, used to post totals to the ledger.

manas.q: What is an analysed petty cash book?

children.note: On the left: money received, i.e. the opening float and each top-up from the bank.
Each payment goes in the total column with date, details and voucher number.
Each payment is also entered in one column: fuel and transport, postage, cleaning, refreshments, sundries.
A VAT-registered business may split out input VAT on eTIMS receipts in a VAT column. Many small offices skip it.
Add down each column, then add the column totals across. The across total must equal the total column.

manas.q: What is cross-casting in a petty cash book?

children.note: Closing balance = receipts minus payments. Bring it down as the opening balance, then add the top-up.
The book feeds the ledger in one entry per period, not one per voucher.
Dr each expense account with its column total / Cr Petty cash with the grand total.

manas.q: What is the entry to post petty cash spending?

children.note: Dr Petty cash / Cr Bank with the amount spent.

manas.q: What is the entry for a petty cash top-up?

children.note: The petty cash balance is a current asset, usually shown with cash and cash equivalents.

children.topic: Is the petty cash book a ledger?
children.note: In many firms it is both: a book of prime entry and the petty cash account itself. Then only the expense side is posted.
Count the cash often and compare with the book. Surprise counts keep everyone honest.
Cash counted + vouchers not yet reimbursed + IOUs = the float. Any gap is a shortage or overage.

manas.q: What does a petty cash reconciliation prove?

children.note: A manager counts the box without warning, in front of the custodian, and both sign the count sheet.

manas.q: Why use surprise petty cash counts?

children.note: List notes and coins by value, add vouchers and IOUs, compare with the float and note any difference.
Dr Cash shortage (expense) / Cr Petty cash. Then investigate why.

manas.q: How is a petty cash shortage recorded?

children.note: Dr Petty cash / Cr Cash over (other income). Often a sign of a missing voucher or change not given.
Many Kenyan offices now pay small spends by M-Pesa. Treat the phone float exactly like a cash box.
Load a fixed float on a company line or business account. Top up only by the amount spent, backed by vouchers.

children.topic: The statement is your receipt book
children.note: Each M-Pesa payment has a transaction code. Write the code on the voucher and match it to the statement.

children.topic: Reconcile the phone like a box
children.note: Phone balance + vouchers spent = float. Charges are an expense too, so give them a bank charges column.
Only the custodian knows the PIN, and the line is in the firm's name. Never use a staff member's personal line.
Small repeat payments to the same number, or money sent to staff and back, can hide theft or limit dodging.
The At-work map on M-Pesa reconciliation shows how to match statements to the books in detail.
Simple controls stop most petty cash fraud. Know the warning signs.
The custodian pays; a manager approves vouchers and signs the top-up; someone else posts the ledger.

manas.q: Which duties should be separated for petty cash?

children.note: The cheque or transfer for the top-up is signed only after a manager checks the vouchers.
Changed amounts, photocopies or handwritten receipts from the same shop time after time.

children.topic: Red flag: just under the limit
children.note: Many payments just below the approval limit suggest a big payment split into small ones.
Top-ups suddenly getting bigger or more frequent with no change in activity.
IOUs that stay in the box for weeks are really unapproved loans.
Before closing the month, make sure all petty cash spending is in the books.
Reimburse on the last day even if the box is not low, so all vouchers are expensed this month.
Do a count, sign the count sheet and file it with the month-end pack.

children.topic: Petty cash in the bank reconciliation?
children.note: No. Petty cash is its own account; only the top-up appears in the bank.
Petty cash is one checklist line in the At-work map on month-end close.
Three linked examples for a Nairobi clinic office. Every figure adds up.
Mwangaza Clinic, Nairobi, starts petty cash on 3 March. Entry: Dr Petty cash KES 20,000 / Cr Bank KES 20,000.

Mon boda boda 300 (T), milk and tea 650 (R); Tue courier 1,200 (P), fuel 2,500 (T); Wed detergent 1,850 (C), matatu 400 (T); Thu water 600 (R); Fri mop 1,100 (C). T=transport, P=postage, C=cleaning, R=refreshments.
Fuel/transport 300+2,500+400 = 3,200. Postage 1,200. Cleaning 1,850+1,100 = 2,950. Refreshments 650+600 = 1,250.
3,200 + 1,200 + 2,950 + 1,250 = 8,600, equal to the total column of KES 8,600. The book cross-casts.
20,000 received - 8,600 paid = KES 11,400 balance carried down.
Top-up KES 8,600. 11,400 + 8,600 = 20,000, so the float is restored.
Post the week to the ledger. Debits equal credits in each entry.
Dr Fuel and transport 3,200; Dr Postage 1,200; Dr Cleaning 2,950; Dr Refreshments 1,250 / Cr Petty cash 8,600. Debits total 8,600.
Dr Petty cash 8,600 / Cr Bank 8,600.
Dr 20,000 (float) - Cr 8,600 (spent) + Dr 8,600 (top-up) = debit balance KES 20,000.
Before the top-up, a surprise count finds KES 11,050 in the box, but the book says 11,400.
Expected 11,400 - counted 11,050 = KES 350 short. Check: 11,050 + vouchers 8,600 = 19,650, 350 below the float.
Dr Cash shortage (expense) 350 / Cr Petty cash 350. Book balance now 11,050, equal to the count.
Look for a lost voucher, an unrecorded IOU, wrong change or a counting error. If a person is to blame, follow HR policy before any recovery.
Errors that cost marks in exams and money at work.
Topping up KES 10,000 instead of the exact amount spent breaks the imprest and hides gaps.
Post the column totals, not 40 tiny entries. It is slower and invites errors.
Petty cash spending is Cr Petty cash. Only the top-up touches the bank.
Always check that the column totals add across to the total column.

children.topic: Treating the float as an expense
children.note: Setting up the float is moving cash from bank to box: asset to asset, not an expense.
Short KASNEB-style questions. Try them before opening the answer bubbles.

Analysis totals: transport 2,100, postage 800, sundries 1,600. Write the ledger and top-up entries.
Dr Transport 2,100; Dr Postage 800; Dr Sundries 1,600 / Cr Petty cash 4,500.
Dr Petty cash 4,500 / Cr Bank 4,500.

children.topic: Q3: Count shows less than book
children.note: Float 20,000; vouchers 14,500; cash counted 5,300. What is the difference and entry?
20,000 - 14,500 = 5,500 expected in the box.
5,500 - 5,300 = KES 200 short. Dr Cash shortage 200 / Cr Petty cash 200.

children.topic: Q4: Two controls over petty cash
children.note: State and explain two controls over a petty cash fund.
1) Imprest system: top-ups only equal approved vouchers, so the float resets. 2) Surprise counts by an independent manager, signed by both.

nodeData.note: A simple guide to keeping a list of everything the business owns for the long term: what to record, how to check it, and how to work out depreciation, disposals and the link to tax.

children.note: A fixed asset register is one list of every long-term item the business owns, with its cost, place, keeper and value. It is the detail behind the fixed asset totals in the books.
Things used in the business for more than one year, like vehicles, computers, furniture and machines. They are not bought to resell.

manas.q: What is a fixed asset?

children.topic: The register: one row per asset
children.note: Each asset gets its own line, like a class register with one name per pupil. A spreadsheet works for a small business; bigger firms use software.

manas.q: What is a fixed asset register?

children.note: You can see what you own, where it is and who has it. Missing or stolen items show up when you check the list against what is really there.
The register works out how much of each asset's cost is used up this year. Those amounts add up to the depreciation charge in the accounts.
If a laptop is stolen or a van is crashed, the register proves you owned it, what it cost and when you bought it. Insurers ask for this.
Auditors pick items from the register and ask to see them, and pick items in the office and look for them on the register. A clean register makes audit quicker and cheaper.
The tax return needs asset costs and dates so tax deductions for assets can be worked out. KRA sets its own rules, separate from book depreciation.
A small pharmacy may own a fridge for vaccines, two computers, a till, shelving and a delivery motorbike. Each one is a row in its register.
These are the usual columns. Add more if your business needs them, but never fewer than the core ones.
A unique number for each asset, also stuck on the item as a label, e.g. FAR-0045. It links the row to the real thing.

manas.q: Why does every asset need a unique tag number?

children.note: What the item is in plain words, plus make, model and serial number, e.g. 'HP laptop 15, serial 5CD1234'.
The group it belongs to, like motor vehicles, computers, furniture, plant and machinery. Each class matches a cost account in the general ledger.

manas.q: What is an asset class or category?

children.note: Where the asset is kept, e.g. 'Westlands branch, front office'. Update it when the item moves.
The person responsible for the asset, e.g. the driver for the van. They sign when they receive it.

manas.q: What is an asset custodian?

children.note: Who sold it and the invoice reference, so you can find the proof of cost and the warranty later.

children.topic: Date bought and date in use
children.note: Purchase date and the date it was ready for use. Depreciation normally starts when it is ready for use.
The price plus costs needed to get it working, like delivery and installation. Leave out VAT you can claim back.

manas.q: What goes into the cost of a fixed asset?

children.note: How many years you expect to use it, and what you expect to sell it for at the end (residual value).
Straight-line or reducing balance, and the rate or number of years. Use the same method for the whole class unless the pattern of use differs.
All the depreciation charged on the asset since it was bought, added up.

manas.q: What is accumulated depreciation?

children.note: Cost minus accumulated depreciation (and minus any impairment). This is what the asset is worth in the books.

manas.q: How do you calculate carrying amount?

children.note: Date sold or scrapped, who bought it, the money received and the gain or loss. The row stays on file, marked disposed.
A short written fixed asset policy tells staff what to record and how. Directors approve it so everyone follows the same rules.
A minimum amount above which an item goes on the register, e.g. KES 50,000. Cheaper items are expensed. The business picks the amount; no law fixes it.

manas.q: What is a capitalisation threshold?

children.note: A KES 18,000 printer under a KES 50,000 threshold: Dr Office expenses 18,000 / Cr Bank 18,000. It does not go on the register.
Some policies capitalise a batch, like 40 office chairs bought together, even if each one is below the threshold. Write down your rule.
Fixing a leak keeps the asset working, so it is an expense. Adding a new floor to a building improves it, so it is added to cost.

manas.q: When is spending on an asset capitalised rather than expensed?

children.note: Set standard lives, e.g. computers 3 years, furniture 8 years, vehicles 5 years. These are your estimates, reviewed each year.
Choose a rule: monthly from the date ready for use, or a full year in the year bought. Apply it the same way every year.
The register is only useful if it matches what is really there. Tags and regular counts keep it honest.

children.topic: Put a tag on every asset
children.note: Stick a durable label or barcode with the asset number on each item, in a place that is easy to see but hard to peel off.
At least once a year, walk around with the register and tick each asset you see. Note its condition and location.

manas.q: What is physical verification of fixed assets?

children.note: From register to floor (does it exist?) and from floor to register (is everything recorded?). Both directions catch different errors.

manas.q: Why check both register-to-floor and floor-to-register?

children.note: Missing item: investigate, then write off if lost. Untagged item: find its invoice and add it. Get a manager to approve each change.
When an asset moves branch or changes custodian, fill a transfer form and update the register the same week.
The count finds tag FAR-0045 missing. After a search and police report, it is written off and an insurance claim is made using register details.
The totals in the register must equal the fixed asset balances in the general ledger (GL). Do this check every month-end.
For each class: total cost in the register = GL cost account, and total accumulated depreciation = GL accumulated depreciation account.

manas.q: What must agree when you reconcile the register to the GL?

children.note: Opening cost + additions − disposals = closing cost. Do the same for accumulated depreciation. Auditors and the notes to the accounts use it.

manas.q: What is the fixed asset movement schedule?

children.note: Register total cost KES 8,450,000; GL KES 8,600,000; gap KES 150,000. A KES 150,000 generator was posted in the GL but never added to the register.
Additions posted to the wrong account, disposals left in the GL, depreciation run in the register but not posted, or typing errors.
Correct the side that is wrong, keep a short note of each fix, and have the reviewer sign the reconciliation.
Worked examples with real numbers. Check each one adds up before you post it.
Laptop KES 95,000 bought on credit. Dr Computer equipment 95,000 / Cr Trade payables 95,000. Add a new row with tag, custodian and date.
Van price KES 2,300,000 plus registration and branding KES 100,000 = cost KES 2,400,000. Fuel and insurance are expenses, not cost.
Yearly depreciation = (cost − residual value) ÷ useful life. Same amount every year.

manas.q: What is the straight-line depreciation formula?

children.note: Cost KES 1,200,000, residual KES 200,000, life 5 years. Each year: 1,000,000 ÷ 5 = KES 200,000.
End of year 1: 1,000,000; year 2: 800,000; year 3: 600,000; year 4: 400,000; year 5: 200,000 (the residual).
Dr Depreciation expense 200,000 / Cr Accumulated depreciation – motor vehicles 200,000.
Year ends 31 December, monthly policy: 200,000 × 9/12 = KES 150,000 in year 1.
Yearly depreciation = rate × carrying amount at the start of the year. The charge gets smaller each year.
